reason: The text demonstrates clear collaboration between Aaron (the leader) and the people working together. The people collectively approach Aaron and request that he 'make gods' for them (וַיִּקָּהֵל הָעָם עַל־אַהֲרֹן). Aaron then instructs them to remove their gold earrings, and the people obey, bringing the gold to him (וַיִּתְפָּרְקוּ כָּל־הָעָם אֶת־נִזְמֵי הַזָּהָב). Aaron takes this gold, fashions it into a calf, and the people jointly engage in worship and celebration of this object. This represents a coordinated effort between a leader and the community working in concert toward a common goal. However, it is crucial to note that this collaboration is presented within a deeply negative moral and theological context—the text frames this joint action as sin and transgression against God's commandments.
